title: Spatiotemporal CV on Air Quality Data with torch Neural Networks
text: companion air-xgboost-bart vignette. uses dataset – DE_RB_2005, daily rural-background PM10 readings 69 German monitoring stations 2005, shipped gstat – fits small feed-forward neural network torch instead tree-based models, folds stcvlite’s spatiotemporal CV schemes way. Neural networks bring two practical concerns tree ensembles mostly sidestep: features must scaled (gradient descent raw longitude/PM10 scales converge well), training iterative, need loop epochs mini-batches rather single fit() call. vignette focuses machinery – scaling within fold avoid leakage, wiring torch::dataset/dataloader stcvlite’s rset splits, reading training curve – rather re-deriving data preparation steps, companion vignette covers detail. vignette two parts. Part 1 (Sections 1-7) fits plain feed-forward network (MLP) row row, exactly like xgboost/BART models companion vignette – every station-day independent observation, network never sees station day row came except lon/lat/time-harmonic features. Part 2 (Sections 8-12) fits graph neural network (GNN) instead: 69 stations become nodes fixed spatial graph, layer lets station’s prediction draw geographic neighbors’ features directly, natural match stcvlite’s station-coordinate CV schemes (lolo, lblo, …) treating every row independent.

code: data("DE_RB_2005", package = "gstat")  air_raw <- as.data.frame(DE_RB_2005) setDT(air_raw) air_raw <- air_raw[!is.na(PM10)] air_raw <- air_raw[, .(   station_id = sp.ID,   coords.x1, coords.x2,   time = as.Date(time),   station_altitude,   PM10 )]  stations_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(   unique(air_raw[, .(station_id, coords.x1, coords.x2)]),   coords = c("coords.x1", "coords.x2"), crs = 32632 ) stations_sf <- sf::st_transform(stations_sf, 4326) station_coords <- data.table(   station_id = stations_sf$station_id,   lon = sf::st_coordinates(stations_sf)[, 1],   lat = sf::st_coordinates(stations_sf)[, 2] )  air_dt <- merge(air_raw, station_coords, by = "station_id") air_dt[, doy := as.integer(format(time, "%j"))] air_dt[, doy_sin := sin(2 * pi * doy / 365)] air_dt[, doy_cos := cos(2 * pi * doy / 365)] air_dt[, c("coords.x1", "coords.x2", "doy") := NULL] setcolorder(air_dt, c("station_id", "lon", "lat", "time"))  feature_cols <- c("lon", "lat", "station_altitude", "doy_sin", "doy_cos") target_col <- "PM10"  nrow(air_dt) air_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(air_dt, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) air_prepped <- suppressWarnings(stcvlite::prep_input(air_sf))

text: Gradient descent needs features comparable scales, target benefits centering . Fitting scaler analysis (training) set – applying parameters assessment (test) set – keeps test-fold information training, exactly model must never see assessment rows. scale response , purely loss starts numerically sane range optimizer; predictions un-scaled back micrograms per cubic meter computing RMSE/MAE.
code: scale_with <- function(x, center, scale) {   scale <- ifelse(scale == 0, 1, scale)   sweep(sweep(x, 2, center, "-"), 2, scale, "/") }  prep_fold_matrices <- function(train, test, feature_cols, target_col) {   x_train_raw <- as.matrix(train[, ..feature_cols])   x_test_raw <- as.matrix(test[, ..feature_cols])    x_center <- colMeans(x_train_raw)   x_scale <- apply(x_train_raw, 2, sd)   y_center <- mean(train[[target_col]])   y_scale <- sd(train[[target_col]])    list(     x_train = scale_with(x_train_raw, x_center, x_scale),     x_test = scale_with(x_test_raw, x_center, x_scale),     y_train = (train[[target_col]] - y_center) / y_scale,     y_center = y_center,     y_scale = y_scale   ) }

code: pm10_net <- torch::nn_module(   classname = "pm10_net",   initialize = function(n_features, hidden = c(16, 8), dropout = 0.1) {     self$fc1 <- torch::nn_linear(n_features, hidden[1])     self$fc2 <- torch::nn_linear(hidden[1], hidden[2])     self$fc3 <- torch::nn_linear(hidden[2], 1)     self$drop <- torch::nn_dropout(dropout)   },   forward = function(x) {     x |>       self$fc1() |>       torch::nnf_relu() |>       self$drop() |>       self$fc2() |>       torch::nnf_relu() |>       self$fc3()   } ) pm10_dataset <- torch::dataset(   name = "pm10_dataset",   initialize = function(x, y) {     self$x <- torch::torch_tensor(x, dtype = torch::torch_float())     self$y <- torch::torch_tensor(matrix(y, ncol = 1), dtype = torch::torch_float())   },   .getitem = function(i) {     list(x = self$x[i, ], y = self$y[i, ])   },   .length = function() {     self$x$size(1)   } )

title: Spatiotemporal CV on Air Quality Data with torch Neural Networks
text: fit_predict_torch() scales fold, trains fixed number epochs Adam MSE loss, returns predictions assessment set (un-scaled) plus per-epoch training loss diagnostics. keep vignette’s build time reasonable, also caps analysis (training) rows fits per fold max_train, subsampling however many fold actually ; full assessment set still scored either way, since prediction single forward pass costs essentially nothing regardless size. smaller sample also reasonable match smaller network (hidden = c(16, 8)) defined – less point training wider net subsample small need much capacity. Three details carry directly dbarts/xgboost fold-fitting companion vignette, just implemented differently: refit scratch every fold’s analysis set (fresh pm10_net() call, weights leak across folds), score fold’s assessment set, record RMSE MAE.
code: fit_predict_torch <- function(train, test, feature_cols, target_col,                                epochs = 15, batch_size = 512, lr = 1e-3,                                max_train = 4000) {   if (nrow(train) > max_train) {     train <- train[sample.int(nrow(train), max_train)]   }   fold <- prep_fold_matrices(train, test, feature_cols, target_col)    model <- pm10_net(n_features = length(feature_cols))   model <- model$to(device = device)   optimizer <- torch::optim_adam(model$parameters, lr = lr)    train_ds <- pm10_dataset(fold$x_train, fold$y_train)   train_dl <- torch::dataloader(train_ds, batch_size = batch_size, shuffle = TRUE)    losses <- numeric(epochs)   for (epoch in seq_len(epochs)) {     model$train()     epoch_loss <- 0     n_seen <- 0     coro::loop(for (batch in train_dl) {       x_b <- batch$x$to(device = device)       y_b <- batch$y$to(device = device)        optimizer$zero_grad()       pred <- model(x_b)       loss <- torch::nnf_mse_loss(pred, y_b)       loss$backward()       optimizer$step()        epoch_loss <- epoch_loss + loss$item() * x_b$size(1)       n_seen <- n_seen + x_b$size(1)     })     losses[epoch] <- epoch_loss / n_seen   }    model$eval()   x_test_t <- torch::torch_tensor(fold$x_test, dtype = torch::torch_float())$to(device = device)   pred_scaled <- torch::with_no_grad(model(x_test_t))   pred <- as.numeric(pred_scaled$to(device = "cpu")) * fold$y_scale + fold$y_center    list(pred = pred, loss_curve = losses) } rmse <- function(actual, pred) sqrt(mean((actual - pred)^2)) mae <- function(actual, pred) mean(abs(actual - pred))  evaluate_rset_torch <- function(rset, cv_mode, epochs = 15) {   per_fold <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(rset)), function(i) {     split <- rset$splits[[i]]     train <- as.data.table(rsample::analysis(split))     test <- as.data.table(rsample::assessment(split))      fit <- fit_predict_torch(train, test, feature_cols, target_col, epochs = epochs)      data.table(       cv_mode = cv_mode,       fold = rset$id[i],       n_test = nrow(test),       rmse = rmse(test[[target_col]], fit$pred),       mae = mae(test[[target_col]], fit$pred),       final_train_loss = fit$loss_curve[epochs]     )   })   rbindlist(per_fold) }

text: Nodes 69 unique stations. Edges connect station k nearest neighbors coordinate distance, found FNN::get.knn() (package stcvlite uses internally one spatial blocking engines). symmetrize result – lists B neighbor, keep -B edge even B’s k nearest happen include – store row-normalized adjacency matrix, node’s graph-convolution input mean neighbors’ features. first version section used plain symmetric-normalized adjacency (shared-weight aggregation Kipf & Welling’s original GCN paper, D^-1/2 (+ ) D^-1/2). graph consistently underperformed row-level MLP: mixing station’s signal eight neighbors one shared weight matrix diluted exactly per-station information (altitude, precise location) mattered . layer fixes giving station’s features neighbors’ features separate weights – GraphSAGE-style mean aggregator – recovered MLP-competitive accuracy testing.
code: station_lookup <- unique(air_dt[, .(station_id, lon, lat, station_altitude)]) setorder(station_lookup, station_id) station_lookup[, station_idx := .I] n_stations <- nrow(station_lookup)  knn <- FNN::get.knn(as.matrix(station_lookup[, .(lon, lat)]), k = 8) adj <- matrix(0, n_stations, n_stations) for (i in seq_len(n_stations)) adj[i, knn$nn.index[i, ]] <- 1 adj <- pmax(adj, t(adj))  a_mean <- adj / rowSums(adj) a_mean_t <- torch::torch_tensor(a_mean, dtype = torch::torch_float())$to(device = device)  cat(sprintf(   "%d stations, %d undirected edges (k = 8 nearest neighbors)\n",   n_stations, sum(adj) / 2 ))

code: day_lookup <- data.table(time = sort(unique(air_dt$time))) day_lookup[, day_idx := .I] day_lookup[, doy := as.integer(format(time, "%j"))] day_lookup[, doy_sin := sin(2 * pi * doy / 365)] day_lookup[, doy_cos := cos(2 * pi * doy / 365)] n_days <- nrow(day_lookup)  air_panel <- copy(air_dt) air_panel[, station_idx := station_lookup$station_idx[match(station_id, station_lookup$station_id)]] air_panel[, day_idx := day_lookup$day_idx[match(time, day_lookup$time)]]  range(air_panel[, .N, by = day_idx]$N) station_feat <- scale(as.matrix(station_lookup[order(station_idx), .(lon, lat, station_altitude)])) day_feat <- as.matrix(day_lookup[order(day_idx), .(doy_sin, doy_cos)])  x_station <- torch::torch_tensor(station_feat, dtype = torch::torch_float()) x_day <- torch::torch_tensor(day_feat, dtype = torch::torch_float())  x_station_b <- x_station$unsqueeze(1)$expand(c(n_days, n_stations, ncol(station_feat))) x_day_b <- x_day$unsqueeze(2)$expand(c(n_days, n_stations, ncol(day_feat))) x_full <- torch::torch_cat(list(x_station_b, x_day_b), dim = 3)  x_full$shape y_full <- matrix(0, n_days, n_stations) obs_mask <- matrix(FALSE, n_days, n_stations) idx_mat <- as.matrix(air_panel[, .(day_idx, station_idx)]) y_full[idx_mat] <- air_panel[[target_col]] obs_mask[idx_mat] <- TRUE  fold_mats <- lapply(cv_indices, function(cv) {   m <- matrix(NA_integer_, n_days, n_stations)   m[idx_mat] <- cv   m })

title: Spatiotemporal CV on Air Quality Data with torch Neural Networks
text: layer computes two linear transforms – one node’s features, one neighbors’ mean features – adds , rather mixing one shared weight matrix: self$register_buffer("a_norm", a_norm) matters: adjacency matrix fixed (learned), registering buffer – rather just assigning self$a_norm <- a_norm – makes model$(device = ...) move along learnable weights, stays device everything else switch GPU. a_norm single (69 x 69) matrix shared every day, torch_matmul(a_norm, x) broadcasts whole batch days x shape (batch, 69, features) – one call aggregates neighbor information every day batch, per-day loop needed.
code: sage_layer <- torch::nn_module(   classname = "sage_layer",   initialize = function(in_features, out_features, a_norm) {     self$lin_self <- torch::nn_linear(in_features, out_features)     self$lin_neigh <- torch::nn_linear(in_features, out_features)     self$register_buffer("a_norm", a_norm)   },   forward = function(x) {     neighbor_mean <- torch::torch_matmul(self$a_norm, x)     self$lin_self(x) + self$lin_neigh(neighbor_mean)   } )  pm10_sage <- torch::nn_module(   classname = "pm10_sage",   initialize = function(n_features, a_norm, hidden = c(32, 16), dropout = 0.05) {     self$gc1 <- sage_layer(n_features, hidden[1], a_norm)     self$gc2 <- sage_layer(hidden[1], hidden[2], a_norm)     self$out <- torch::nn_linear(hidden[2], 1)     self$drop <- torch::nn_dropout(dropout)   },   forward = function(x) {     x |>       self$gc1() |>       torch::nnf_relu() |>       self$drop() |>       self$gc2() |>       torch::nnf_relu() |>       self$out()   } )

Days belong entirely assessment set given fold (e.g. every day held-lbto block) skipped training used scoring. Note “batch” costs versus Section 5: MLP’s dataloader iterates mini-batches individual rows, even capping training rows max_train = 4000 per fold keep Section 6 fast, GCN’s mini-batches – individual days, 365 , one single matrix multiply 69x69 adjacency shared across whole dataset – need subsampling run quickly. Refitting sum(sapply(cv_indices, max)) folds across four schemes takes well minute despite using five times epoch count (80 vs. 15), number gradient steps scales number days, number station-day rows.
code: masked_mse <- function(pred, target, mask) {   ((pred - target)^2 * mask)$sum() / mask$sum() }  fit_predict_gcn <- function(cv_mode, fold_id, epochs = 80, batch_days = 32, lr = 0.01) {   fold_mat <- fold_mats[[cv_mode]]   train_mask_mat <- obs_mask & !is.na(fold_mat) & (fold_mat != fold_id)   test_mask_mat  <- obs_mask & !is.na(fold_mat) & (fold_mat == fold_id)    y_center <- mean(y_full[train_mask_mat])   y_scale <- sd(y_full[train_mask_mat])   y_scaled <- (y_full - y_center) / y_scale   y_scaled[!obs_mask] <- 0    y_t <- torch::torch_tensor(y_scaled, dtype = torch::torch_float())$to(device = device)   train_mask_t <- torch::torch_tensor(train_mask_mat * 1, dtype = torch::torch_float())$to(device = device)    train_days <- which(rowSums(train_mask_mat) > 0)   test_days <- which(rowSums(test_mask_mat) > 0)    model <- pm10_sage(n_features = x_full$shape[3], a_norm = a_mean_t)   model <- model$to(device = device)   optimizer <- torch::optim_adam(model$parameters, lr = lr)    losses <- numeric(epochs)   for (epoch in seq_len(epochs)) {     model$train()     perm <- sample(train_days)     batches <- split(perm, ceiling(seq_along(perm) / batch_days))     epoch_loss <- 0     for (b in batches) {       optimizer$zero_grad()       x_b <- x_full[b, , ]$to(device = device)       if (length(b) == 1) x_b <- x_b$unsqueeze(1)       pred <- model(x_b)$squeeze(3)       y_b <- y_t[b, ]       m_b <- train_mask_t[b, ]       if (length(b) == 1) {         y_b <- y_b$unsqueeze(1)         m_b <- m_b$unsqueeze(1)       }       loss <- masked_mse(pred, y_b, m_b)       loss$backward()       optimizer$step()       epoch_loss <- epoch_loss + loss$item() * length(b)     }     losses[epoch] <- epoch_loss / length(perm)   }    model$eval()   x_test <- x_full[test_days, , ]$to(device = device)   if (length(test_days) == 1) x_test <- x_test$unsqueeze(1)   pred_scaled <- torch::with_no_grad(model(x_test)$squeeze(3))   pred_mat <- as.matrix(pred_scaled$to(device = "cpu")) * y_scale + y_center    actual_mat <- y_full[test_days, , drop = FALSE]   mask_mat <- test_mask_mat[test_days, , drop = FALSE]    list(     pred = pred_mat[mask_mat == 1],     actual = actual_mat[mask_mat == 1],     loss_curve = losses   ) }  evaluate_gcn <- function(cv_mode, epochs = 80) {   n_folds <- max(cv_indices[[cv_mode]])   per_fold <- lapply(seq_len(n_folds), function(k) {     fit <- fit_predict_gcn(cv_mode, k, epochs = epochs)     data.table(       cv_mode = cv_mode,       fold = k,       n_test = length(fit$pred),       rmse = rmse(fit$actual, fit$pred),       mae = mae(fit$actual, fit$pred)     )   })   rbindlist(per_fold) } results_gcn <- rbindlist(lapply(names(cv_indices), evaluate_gcn))  summary_gcn <- results_gcn[, .(   n_folds = uniqueN(fold),   mean_rmse = mean(rmse),   mean_mae = mean(mae) ), by = cv_mode]  knitr::kable(summary_gcn[order(cv_mode)], digits = 2)

text: DE_RB_2005 spacetime::STSDF – sparse space-time object holding one PM10 measurement per station-day, plus per-station metadata elevation. flatten long table .data.frame(), drop missing readings, keep station identifier, coordinates (originally UTM zone 32N), date, station altitude (genuine predictor background PM10), response.
code: data("DE_RB_2005", package = "gstat") air_raw <- as.data.frame(DE_RB_2005) setDT(air_raw) air_raw <- air_raw[!is.na(PM10)] air_raw <- air_raw[, .(   station_id = sp.ID,   coords.x1, coords.x2,   time = as.Date(time),   station_altitude,   PM10 )]  cat(sprintf(   "%d station-day observations across %d stations\n",   nrow(air_raw), uniqueN(air_raw$station_id) )) #> 23230 station-day observations across 69 stations

code: stations_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(   unique(air_raw[, .(station_id, coords.x1, coords.x2)]),   coords = c("coords.x1", "coords.x2"), crs = 32632 ) stations_sf <- sf::st_transform(stations_sf, 4326) station_coords <- data.table(   station_id = stations_sf$station_id,   lon = sf::st_coordinates(stations_sf)[, 1],   lat = sf::st_coordinates(stations_sf)[, 2] )  air_dt <- merge(air_raw, station_coords, by = "station_id") air_dt[, doy := as.integer(format(time, "%j"))] air_dt[, doy_sin := sin(2 * pi * doy / 365)] air_dt[, doy_cos := cos(2 * pi * doy / 365)] air_dt[, c("coords.x1", "coords.x2", "doy") := NULL] setcolorder(air_dt, c("station_id", "lon", "lat", "time"))  str(air_dt) #> Classes 'data.table' and 'data.frame':   23230 obs. of  8 variables: #>  $ station_id      : chr  "DEBB053" "DEBB053" "DEBB053" "DEBB053" ... #>  $ lon             : num  14 14 14 14 14 ... #>  $ lat             : num  52.6 52.6 52.6 52.6 52.6 ... #>  $ time            : Date, format: "2005-01-01" "2005-01-02" ... #>  $ station_altitude: int  88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 ... #>  $ PM10            : num  27.17 10.21 6.75 12.56 13.67 ... #>  $ doy_sin         : num  0.0172 0.0344 0.0516 0.0688 0.086 ... #>  $ doy_cos         : num  1 0.999 0.999 0.998 0.996 ... #>  - attr(*, ".internal.selfref")=<pointer: 0x55c01b5ccf20>  #>  - attr(*, "sorted")= chr "station_id"

(prep_input() calls sf::st_point_on_surface() internally, warns point geometries even though coordinates returns exact – safe ignore .)

title: Spatiotemporal CV on gstat's Air Quality Data with xgboost and BART
text: generate_spt_index() turns station coordinates (, optionally, time) single grouping key. "spatial" mode collapses one key per station; "spatiotemporal" mode every station-day gets key. generate_block_sp_index() uses lon/lat columns group stations contiguous spatial blocks (DBSCAN default), clustering unique station location regardless many days observed. mechanism behind "lblo" "lblto" schemes – six blocks stations, chosen purely coordinates:
code: air_spatial <- generate_spt_index(air_prepped, mode = "spatial") air_spt <- generate_spt_index(air_prepped, mode = "spatiotemporal")  cat(sprintf(   "unique spatial keys: %d (= number of stations)\n",   uniqueN(air_spatial$sp_index) )) #> unique spatial keys: 69 (= number of stations) cat(sprintf(   "unique spatiotemporal keys: %d (= number of rows)\n",   uniqueN(air_spt$sp_index) )) #> unique spatiotemporal keys: 23230 (= number of rows) air_blocks <- generate_block_sp_index(air_prepped, cv_fold = 6) table(air_blocks$sp_index) #>  #>    1    2    3    4    5    6  #> 3380 2873 5443 3615 5194 2725 plot_cv_folds(air_blocks, air_blocks$sp_index, max_points = 5000)

what: 4. Every cross-validation scheme, side by side
title: Spatiotemporal CV on gstat's Air Quality Data with xgboost and BART
text: generate_cv_index() implements seven schemes (see package README full description acronym). build compare fold structure induce 23,230-row dataset: leave-one-station-(lolo) leave-one-day-(loto) hold one coordinate time; lolto plain leave-one-row-; lblo/lbto/lblto group stations /days contiguous blocks; random naive baseline. lolo lblo/lbto/lblto hold whole stations blocks, every fold tests extrapolation space /time. loto lolto produce far , much smaller folds (365 23,230 respectively) – faithful “leave-one-” definition, many refit two models vignette. generate indices show fold structure, evaluate models five schemes , using helper code apply identically loto/lolto given enough time.
code: cv_indices <- list(   lolo   = generate_cv_index(air_prepped, cv_mode = "lolo"),   loto   = generate_cv_index(air_prepped, cv_mode = "loto"),   lolto  = generate_cv_index(air_prepped, cv_mode = "lolto"),   lblo   = generate_cv_index(air_prepped, cv_mode = "lblo", cv_fold = 6),   lbto   = generate_cv_index(air_prepped, cv_mode = "lbto", cv_fold = 6),   lblto  = generate_cv_index(air_prepped, cv_mode = "lblto", sp_fold = 4, t_fold = 3),   random = generate_cv_index(air_prepped, cv_mode = "random", cv_fold = 5) )  fold_summary <- rbindlist(lapply(names(cv_indices), function(m) {   tb <- table(cv_indices[[m]])   data.table(     cv_mode = m,     n_folds = length(tb),     min_fold_size = min(tb),     max_fold_size = max(tb)   ) })) knitr::kable(fold_summary)

title: Spatiotemporal CV on gstat's Air Quality Data with xgboost and BART
text: models use feature set – station coordinates, altitude, seasonal harmonics – refit independently analysis set every fold, scored fold’s assessment set. convert_cv_index_rset() turns fold-assignment vector tidymodels-compatible rset; rsample::analysis() rsample::assessment() pull train/test tables split. evaluate_rset() loops every fold given rset, fits models, records RMSE/MAE: run five schemes: random (optimistic) baseline, lolo pure spatial extrapolation unseen stations, lblo block-wise spatial extrapolation, lbto pure temporal extrapolation unseen time blocks, lblto combined spatiotemporal block extrapolation. lolo alone means refitting models 69 times; laptop section takes roughly two three minutes.
code: feature_cols <- c("lon", "lat", "station_altitude", "doy_sin", "doy_cos") target_col <- "PM10"  fit_predict_xgb <- function(train, test) {   dtrain <- xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(     data = as.matrix(train[, ..feature_cols]),     label = train[[target_col]]   )   fit <- xgboost::xgb.train(     data = dtrain,     nrounds = 150,     params = list(       objective = "reg:squarederror",       max_depth = 4, eta = 0.1, subsample = 0.8     ),     verbose = 0   )   predict(fit, as.matrix(test[, ..feature_cols])) }  fit_predict_bart <- function(train, test) {   fit <- dbarts::bart(     x.train = as.matrix(train[, ..feature_cols]),     y.train = train[[target_col]],     x.test = as.matrix(test[, ..feature_cols]),     ntree = 50, ndpost = 300, nskip = 100,     verbose = FALSE, keeptrees = FALSE   )   fit$yhat.test.mean } rmse <- function(actual, pred) sqrt(mean((actual - pred)^2)) mae <- function(actual, pred) mean(abs(actual - pred))  evaluate_rset <- function(rset, cv_mode) {   per_fold <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(rset)), function(i) {     split <- rset$splits[[i]]     train <- as.data.table(rsample::analysis(split))     test <- as.data.table(rsample::assessment(split))      pred_xgb <- fit_predict_xgb(train, test)     pred_bart <- fit_predict_bart(train, test)      data.table(       cv_mode = cv_mode,       fold = rset$id[i],       n_test = nrow(test),       engine = c("xgboost", "bart"),       rmse = c(rmse(test[[target_col]], pred_xgb), rmse(test[[target_col]], pred_bart)),       mae = c(mae(test[[target_col]], pred_xgb), mae(test[[target_col]], pred_bart))     )   })   rbindlist(per_fold) } rset_random <- convert_cv_index_rset(cv_indices$random, air_prepped, cv_mode = "random") rset_lolo   <- convert_cv_index_rset(cv_indices$lolo, air_prepped, cv_mode = "lolo") rset_lblo   <- convert_cv_index_rset(cv_indices$lblo, air_prepped, cv_mode = "lblo") rset_lbto   <- convert_cv_index_rset(cv_indices$lbto, air_prepped, cv_mode = "lbto") rset_lblto  <- convert_cv_index_rset(cv_indices$lblto, air_prepped, cv_mode = "lblto")  results <- rbindlist(list(   evaluate_rset(rset_random, "random"),   evaluate_rset(rset_lolo, "lolo"),   evaluate_rset(rset_lblo, "lblo"),   evaluate_rset(rset_lbto, "lbto"),   evaluate_rset(rset_lblto, "lblto") ))

title: Spatiotemporal CV on gstat's Air Quality Data with xgboost and BART
text: Averaging RMSE within scheme/engine combination shows much CV scheme changes apparent accuracy:
code: summary_tbl <- results[, .(   n_folds = uniqueN(fold),   mean_rmse = mean(rmse),   mean_mae = mean(mae) ), by = .(cv_mode, engine)]  knitr::kable(summary_tbl[order(cv_mode, engine)], digits = 2) plotly::plot_ly(   data = results,   x = ~cv_mode, y = ~rmse, color = ~engine,   type = "box" ) |>   plotly::layout(     yaxis = list(title = "Fold RMSE (PM10, ug/m3)"),     xaxis = list(title = "CV scheme"),     boxmode = "group"   )

title: Lightweight rsample extension for spatiotemporal cross-validation
text: Spatial blocks group nearby locations together entire block ends fold, preventing spatial autocorrelation leaking training test sets. generate_block_sp_index() attaches sp_index column covariate table supports three block-definition strategies.

title: Lightweight rsample extension for spatiotemporal cross-validation
text: cv_fold supplied without blocks, coordinates clustered DBSCAN.
code: # Create 5 spatial clusters based on (lon, lat) spdat_block <- generate_block_sp_index(spdat, cv_fold = 5) spdat_block[, c("lon", "lat", "sp_index")] #> lon and lat columns alongside integer cluster ids 1–5

title: Lightweight rsample extension for spatiotemporal cross-validation
text: Pass length-2 numeric vector cut bounding box rectangular cells.
code: # ~5° × 5° grid cells spdat_grid <- generate_block_sp_index(spdat, blocks = c(5, 5)) spdat_grid[, c("lon", "lat", "sp_index")]

title: Lightweight rsample extension for spatiotemporal cross-validation
text: Provide sf SpatVector polygon layer whose features define block boundaries (e.g. states, counties, hydrological units). block_id argument names column uniquely identifies feature.
code: library(sf)  # Example: U.S. state polygons (replace with your own polygon layer) state_polygons <- sf::read_sf("path/to/states.gpkg")  spdat_poly <- generate_block_sp_index(   spdat,   blocks   = state_polygons,   block_id = "STUSPS"   # unique state abbreviation column ) spdat_poly[, c("lon", "lat", "sp_index")]

title: Lightweight rsample extension for spatiotemporal cross-validation
text: generate_cv_index() returns integer (factor) fold-assignment vector one value per row input. Pass vector together data convert_cv_index_rset() obtain tidymodels-compatible rset object.

title: Lightweight rsample extension for spatiotemporal cross-validation
text: unique location forms one fold; time steps location held together.
code: data(spdat)  cv_lolo <- generate_cv_index(spdat, cv_mode = "lolo") # cv_lolo is an integer vector of length nrow(spdat) # unique values == number of unique locations (100)  rset_lolo <- convert_cv_index_rset(cv_lolo, spdat, cv_mode = "lolo") rset_lolo

title: Lightweight rsample extension for spatiotemporal cross-validation
text: unique time step one fold; locations time step held .
code: cv_loto <- generate_cv_index(spdat, cv_mode = "loto") # unique values == number of unique time steps (120)  rset_loto <- convert_cv_index_rset(cv_loto, spdat, cv_mode = "loto")

title: Lightweight rsample extension for spatiotemporal cross-validation
text: Every single row becomes fold (standard LOO). Suitable small datasets.
code: cv_lolto <- generate_cv_index(spdat, cv_mode = "lolto")

title: Lightweight rsample extension for spatiotemporal cross-validation
text: Spatially contiguous groups locations form fold. Uses k-means clustering internally cv_fold integer.
code: cv_lblo <- generate_cv_index(spdat, cv_mode = "lblo", cv_fold = 5)  rset_lblo <- convert_cv_index_rset(cv_lblo, spdat, cv_mode = "lblo") rset_lblo #> # 5-fold spatial block CV  # You can also supply pre-built polygon blocks: # cv_lblo_poly <- generate_cv_index( #   spdat, cv_mode = "lblo", #   blocks = state_polygons, block_id = "STUSPS" # )

title: Lightweight rsample extension for spatiotemporal cross-validation
text: Consecutive time steps grouped cv_fold temporal chunks.
code: cv_lbto <- generate_cv_index(spdat, cv_mode = "lbto", cv_fold = 6)  rset_lbto <- convert_cv_index_rset(cv_lbto, spdat, cv_mode = "lbto")

title: Lightweight rsample extension for spatiotemporal cross-validation
text: Combines spatial temporal blocking. fold one cell sp_fold * t_fold grid spatiotemporal blocks.
code: cv_lblto <- generate_cv_index(   spdat,   cv_mode = "lblto",   sp_fold = 5,   t_fold  = 4 ) # up to 5 × 4 = 20 unique spatiotemporal blocks  rset_lblto <- convert_cv_index_rset(cv_lblto, spdat, cv_mode = "lblto")

title: Lightweight rsample extension for spatiotemporal cross-validation
text: Plain random k-fold assignment included baseline.
code: cv_random <- generate_cv_index(spdat, cv_mode = "random", cv_fold = 10)  rset_random <- convert_cv_index_rset(cv_random, spdat, cv_mode = "random")

title: Lightweight rsample extension for spatiotemporal cross-validation
text: plot_cv_folds() renders 3-D scatter (lon × lat × time) colored fold, useful quickly checking spatial/temporal structure captured.
code: if (requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE)) {   # Spatial block CV — clusters should appear as distinct spatial patches   plot_cv_folds(spdat, cv_lblo)    # Spatiotemporal block CV   plot_cv_folds(spdat, cv_lblto) }

text: rset objects returned convert_cv_index_rset() fully compatible tune workflows packages.
code: library(rsample) library(parsnip) library(workflows) library(tune)  # Define a simple linear regression model lm_spec <- linear_reg() |> set_engine("lm")  wflow <- workflow() |>   add_formula(y ~ x1 + x2) |>   add_model(lm_spec)  # Evaluate using spatial block CV cv_results_lblo <- fit_resamples(wflow, resamples = rset_lblo) collect_metrics(cv_results_lblo)  # # A tibble: 2 × 6 #   .metric .estimator   mean     n std_err .config         #   <chr>   <chr>       <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>           # 1 rmse    standard   5.24       5 0.0108  pre0_mod0_post0 # 2 rsq     standard   0.0116     5 0.00110 pre0_mod0_post0   # Evaluate using spatiotemporal block CV cv_results_lbto <- fit_resamples(wflow, resamples = rset_lbto) collect_metrics(cv_results_lbto)  # # A tibble: 2 × 6 #   .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err .config         #   <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>           # 1 rmse    standard   5.53      6 1.28    pre0_mod0_post0 # 2 rsq     standard   0.303     6 0.00171 pre0_mod0_post0  # Evaluate using spatiotemporal block CV cv_results_lblto <- fit_resamples(wflow, resamples = rset_lblto) collect_metrics(cv_results_lblto)  # # A tibble: 2 × 6 #   .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err .config         #   <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>           # 1 rmse    standard   5.02     20 0.540   pre0_mod0_post0 # 2 rsq     standard   0.155    20 0.00665 pre0_mod0_post0
